title: Exhaustive searches for Williams numbers: the four-prime case and a general 10^24 bound — code, logs, certificates and manuscript
description: Source code, per-block logs, survivor dumps, certification records and the manuscript (with its exploratory supplementary note) for the paper Exhaustive searches for Williams numbers: the four-prime case and a general 10^24 bound. A Williams number is a squarefree composite n that is both Carmichael ((p-1) | (n-1) for every prime p | n) and Lucas-Carmichael ((p+1) | (n+1) for every p | n); none is known. The repository contains the C enumerator for four-prime Williams numbers (certified exclusions: none with n ≤ 10^30, none with smallest prime ≤ 500,000), the factor-and-test scan of all 308,279,939 Carmichael numbers below 10^24 (no Williams number; full histogram of matching primes), the polynomial-family searches, the test suite, and the review record. Third-party input tabulations (Shallue-Webster via Stamm-Wilbrandt, Goutier, Suteu) are cited and identified by SHA-256, not redistributed.
